extracted.intended_audience: researchers, science policy makers, grant applicants, and scholars of peer review and research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of how independent reviewer selection and inter-reviewer disagreement affect grant award outcomes; reports an experiment re-reviewing 150 NSF proposals showing substantial chance effects and no systematic reviewer-selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependence of grant funding on chance
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting a research grant depends to a significant extent on chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper reports an experiment in which 150 proposals submitted to the National Science Foundation were evaluated independently by a new set of reviewers; results indicate that whether or not a proposal is funded often depends upon which reviewers happen to be selected for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of disagreement among eligible reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree of disagreement within the population of eligible reviewers is such that whether or not a proposal is funded depends in a large proportion of cases upon which reviewers happen to be selected for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-reviewer disagreement is a key measurable dimension of peer review reliability; high disagreement implies low consensus and greater outcome variability. Assessments of panels or selection procedures should measure and account for this disagreement when interpreting funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment for systematic bias in reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: No evidence of systematic bias in the selection of NSF reviewers was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations of reviewer selection procedures should test for systematic bias (e.g., demographic, institutional, topical); in this study the experiment did not find such bias, suggesting that observed outcome variability arose primarily from reviewer disagreement rather than selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent re-review experiments to evaluate peer review reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: An experiment re-evaluating the same set of proposals by a new set of reviewers is used to estimate the role of chance and consensus in funding outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological implication: replicate or reassign reviews independently to quantify how much funding variability is due to reviewer selection versus systematic factors. Such experimental designs provide empirical evidence about reliability and fairness of grant peer review systems.
